meaning: 수호 (秀浩, Suho) joins 수 (秀, su), meaning outstanding, with 호 (浩, ho), meaning broad, painting a hope for someone whose excellence stretches wide and generous, never narrow or small — a mind and heart with room enough for great things. Spoken aloud, it flows softly, two open syllables rising and settling, gentle on the tongue yet clear and crisp. Abroad, it echoes comfortably beside the English name Shun, easy for new friends to catch, while still carrying its own quiet, expansive strength wherever it is spoken.
surname_desc: Ko (高) is Korea's 22nd most common surname at about 0.9%. The Jeju Ko clan is legendary — one of the three founding families said to have emerged from the earth on Jeju Island.

short: Someone earnest who rises bright like the dawn
meaning: 건우 (虔旭, Geonu) combines 건 (虔, geon), "sincere and devoted," with 우 (旭, u), "the rising morning sun." It pictures someone earnest who rises bright like the dawn. Dependable yet warm, 건우 is a long-time favorite: 건 gives an honest, solid feel, while 우 is one of the most loved endings, as in 준우 (Junu) and 지우 (Jiu). Comfortable and well-loved, it's easy on the ear.

short: Mountaintop, the highest point in native Korean
meaning: 마루 (Maru) — above all, this is the native Korean word for "mountaintop, the highest point (sky)." The characters 마 (瑪, "agate") and 루 (婁, "star") echo beneath, but the native meaning leads: someone who shines like a star from the highest place. Round and spirited with no final consonants, it's a bright, beloved boy's name with a fresh native ring.
surname_desc: Lee (李) is Korea's second most common surname at about 14.7% of the population. Its most famous lineage, the Jeonju Lee clan, founded the Joseon Dynasty and ruled Korea for over 500 years.

short: Someone good for the world
meaning: 로운 (鷺夽, Roun) joins 로 (鷺, ro), "heron, egret," with 운 (夽, un), "lofty and high." It evokes the native word 이로운 ("beneficial"), suggesting someone good for the world. K-pop and drama fans may recall the actor Rowoon (SF9) — a trendy, refined impression with a soft, modern ending.
surname_desc: Seo (徐) is Korea's 13th most common surname at about 1.5%. The Dalseong and Icheon Seo clans produced distinguished scholars, including famed Joseon-era prime ministers.

short: Someone bright as noon and high in virtue
meaning: 오성 (旿聖, Oseong) pairs 오 (旿, o), "the bright midday sun," with 성 (聖, seong), "virtuous and saintly." It pictures someone bright as noon and high in virtue. Solid and upright, it recalls Oseong of the famous Joseon duo "Oseong and Haneum," wise and full of wit. Brightness and virtue in a clever, dependable name.

short: A broad, auspicious path through life
meaning: 상호 (祥浩, Sangho) joins 상 (祥, sang), meaning auspicious, with 호 (浩, ho), meaning broad, painting the picture of a wide, fortunate path opening before someone — a life meant to expand generously, carrying good omen into whatever it touches. It shares its rhythm with names like 상현, 상윤, 지호, and 윤호, cousins in sound and spirit. Spoken aloud, Sangho feels compact yet open, its consonants crisp, its vowels wide and easy, landing gently on the ear — not unlike Satoshi abroad, familiar in shape though different in root, a name that travels well while staying rooted in its own bright meaning.
surname_desc: Ahn (安) is Korea's 17th most common surname at about 1.3%. Meaning 'peace,' it's borne by national heroes like independence activist Ahn Jung-geun — the Sunheung Ahn clan is its main lineage.

short: One who carries greatness forward with steady hands
meaning: 대승 (大承, Daeseung) joins 대 (大, dae), meaning great, with 승 (承, seung), meaning to carry on, painting a hope that someone will bear forward something vast — a family's spirit, a lineage of effort — with steady, capable hands. It suggests not just greatness inherited, but greatness continued and renewed. Spoken aloud, the name feels open and confident, its vowels wide and unhurried, its consonants crisp without harshness. Abroad, it settles comfortably beside other names, carrying a firm, resonant rhythm that feels natural in either language.
surname_desc: Heo (許) is Korea's 29th most common surname at about 0.6%. Legend holds the Gimhae Heo clan descends from Queen Heo Hwang-ok, an ancient princess said to have sailed from India to marry King Suro.

short: Someone bright as the east with a sky-wide heart
meaning: 동민 (東旻, Dongmin) joins 동 (東, dong), "east, sunrise direction," with 민 (旻, min), "the vast sky." It's a boy's name meaning someone bright as the east with a sky-wide heart. The 민 syllable is beloved across names, as in 지민 (Jimin) and 서민 (Seomin) — a bright, upstanding, trendy impression.

short: Someone refined, with eloquence
meaning: 아론 (雅論, Aron) joins 아 (雅, a), "elegant and refined," with 론 (論, ron), "discourse, wisdom." It matches "Aaron," the biblical first high priest — globally resonant. K-pop fans may recall Aron of NU'EST. It's a boy's name, refined and international — a polished impression.

short: Someone victorious and broad-minded
meaning: 승범 (勝汎, Seungbeom) joins 승 (勝, seung), "to win, to excel," with 범 (汎, beom), "broad, far-reaching." It's a boy's name meaning someone victorious and broad-minded. 승 symbolizes victory; 범 lends a magnanimous, big-hearted nature — a confident, refreshing impression.
surname_desc: Min (閔) is Korea's 41st most common surname at about 0.2%. The Yeoheung Min clan produced several Joseon queens, including Empress Myeongseong.

short: Someone sky-wide who overcomes all
meaning: 민승 (旻勝, Minseung) joins 민 (旻, min), "the vast sky," with 승 (勝, seung), "to win, to excel." It's a boy's name meaning someone sky-wide who overcomes all. The 승 syllable, as in 승우 (Seungu) and 승현 (Seunghyeon), symbolizes victory — a confident, spirited impression.
